payload.message:
JIRA sprint task allocation. Each agent chooses at most one micro-task (or skips). Maximize tasks completed, prefer higher-priority tasks, then minimize total cost. Avoid duplicate task selections and infeasible assignments.

NOTE: If environment.assignment_filling=true and an agent fails to assign a variable, the environment will fill any remaining unassigned variables with a uniform-random allowed assignment when producing final results.

This blackboard is a private communication channel.
Participants: Allyn, Dorinda, Guadalupe, Guillermina, Rena, Sean

payload.content: Sean here. My private costs are lowest on ISSUE-0002::review (1.63), then ISSUE-0002::test (2.28), ISSUE-0001::triage (2.83), ISSUE-0002::implement (3.26). All tasks are medium priority, so the tiebreaker is cost. Proposal: I claim ISSUE-0002::review. Everyone else, please pick a distinct task from the list (no duplicates) and favor your lowest-cost option. Suggest ISSUE-0002::test or ISSUE-0001::triage for others if they are cheapest for them. Reply if you object or have a conflict.

Rena here. My private costs: ISSUE-0002::review 1.54, ISSUE-0002::test 2.16, ISSUE-0002::implement 3.08, ISSUE-0001::triage 3.25. Sean, since all tasks are medium priority, I'll concede ISSUE-0002::review to you (your cost 1.63). Combined, that's cheaper than me taking review and you taking test (1.54+2.28=3.82 vs 1.63+2.16=3.79). I'm claiming ISSUE-0002::test (cost 2.16). Others: please pick from ISSUE-0002::implement, ISSUE-0001::triage, or the ISSUE-0001 review/docs/test/implement tasks, avoiding ours. (planning, iter=1)
